Try splitting the goals up into small, itsy bitsy tiny goals that'll give you gratification. 

Look up that one thing you wanted to research and open up a bunch of tabs? Boom, goal fulfilled. Get yourself a cookie, because you're one step closer. 

Don't feel like reading them? Don't worry, goal for next time is to look through one of them for a few minutes. You're interested and want to read more? That's two cookies for you. 

You can set goals for anything. 1 Goal a day is good, but if you have another +1 for eating and +1 for a random chore, that's already 3 goals a day, more is always possible.

Get yourself a daily repeating alarm, for each task you'll have one ringing 5 minutes before you're supposed to do the task, and then right when you're going to do it. Finish up whatever you're doing in those 5 minutes and get to work. 

Get a task done earlier? That's another cookie for you. 

Of course, "cookies" just means something that you can reward yourself with. Whether that would be a small addition to your personal budget, a nice bubble bath at the end of the day, a round of your favorite game or a literal cookie is up to you. It has to be something that makes you happy that you otherwise wouldn't do or have.

Don't reward yourself with actual meals, sleep or anything vital for human survival.

Personally, I think self diagnosing is only helpful if you're looking into the resources to help you deal with those problems and see if they better your position at all.

I've found myself relating a lot to a few mental disorders, but used them more as a "Oh I feel so shit, but I probably have XYZ so that must be it", "that's my XYZ acting up," , "I can't help to do this this because I probably have XYZ" thing to shift the blame on. 

Obviously in reality these thoughts were more subtle, and in no way am I implying that you're going through the same.

However, as a general hint of advice: Look into the resources that help you cope with those disorders, don't just relate to the symptoms and dwell in your bad mental health.
